properties.name: Nine dangling TemporalFact.subject_id references repointed, and the rename story behind four of them was false
properties.rationale:
🛑 THE RECORDED CAUSE FOR FOUR OF THESE WAS FALSE, AND CORRECTING IT MATTERS BECAUSE A PROPOSED DECISION RESTS ON IT. `dec:a-restore-reports-an-unresolvable-reference-rather-than-refusing-it` says the nine are "five instances of a `prj:`/`proj:` typo, four capabilities renamed after the fact was written", and the INVALIDATES note on `fact:defect-a-property-naming-a-node-is-unguarded-while-edges-are-not` repeats it: "four were VALID WHEN WRITTEN and broke later when the target was renamed".

MEASURED 2026-08-29, and it refutes that. `git log -S '"node_id": "cap:link-artifacts"' -- docs/design/reflow2.json` returns ZERO commits, and the same for `cap:reconcile-artifacts`, `cap:thin-install` and `cap:gap-to-prompt`. The identical probe against a real capability (`cap:adopt`) returns one. **These ids never existed as nodes.** They were wrong when written — the same class as the five typos, not rename-rot.

WHY IT CHANGES SOMETHING RATHER THAN BEING A TIDY-UP: that decision argues the write-time guard cannot reach the real cause, because "the renames that produce most real dangles are unreachable by ANY write-time check". On this graph there were no renames. All nine would have been refused at write time by the guard #366 shipped, which weakens one leg of the argument for reporting rather than refusing on import. THE DECISION'S MAIN ARGUMENT IS UNTOUCHED and still looks right — an import ASSERTS NOTHING, it reproduces a state the document is evidence of, and refusing there substitutes the tool's judgement for a reality it is being handed. Only the supporting claim about renames is withdrawn, and it is withdrawn on evidence rather than on preference.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: that renames never break references — only that none of THIS graph's nine came from one, so the rename case remains hypothetical here rather than demonstrated. The separate detection defect this work surfaced is recorded at `fact:a-dangling-reference-is-only-detected-when-the-node-is-also-edgeless`.
properties.subject: record
properties.summary: All nine dangling `TemporalFact.subject_id` values on this graph now resolve. Five were the `prj:`/`proj:` typo and went to `proj:reflow2`, the design's only Project. The other four named capabilities that do not exist, and each was repointed by reading the fact and confirming the target owns the thing the fact is about: `fact:defect-append-only-volatility-exempts-a-structural-rewrite` and `fact:defect-link-artifact-has-no-type-for-a-test-source` → `cap:artifact-declares-its-own-shape`, whose own description covers exactly this ("an artifact declares what it stands for and how its content behaves", and the shared failure that "the graph held two OPPOSITE states that produced an identical reading" — the volatility exemption and the missing `test` enum value are both instances); `fact:defect-kit-manifest-drift-is-invisible-to-ci` → `cap:kit`, established not by resemblance but because `ver:kit-manifest-agrees` VERIFIES it; `fact:gap-to-prompt-tells-the-agent-to-strip-the-vocabulary-its-own-description-says-to-keep` → `cap:gap-carries-a-reading`, whose name ends "in their own language", which is the clause the fact says the emitted template contradicts. Written through `create_nodes`, so #366's `node_ref` guard validated every new target as a side effect of accepting the write.
